data.narrative:
Cellares is a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Fabian Gerlinghaus and Omar Kurdi that has raised $350M+. Valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 8 private and 3 public companies in the Biotech & Health sector, including same-stage comparables Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and New Limit.

Two valuation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method, using $12M as a total-raised proxy, applies a 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to imply $20M. The peer-median approach anchors to three same-sector, same-stage private comparables with a median valuation of $3.8B, spanning a range of $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Cellares' revenue is not on file; the sector median P/S for Biotech & Health public companies is 5.5x across three tickers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L), but this requires disclosed revenue to be operationalized.

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $17M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $1.9B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in whether Cellares scales toward the peer median or remains below it. Key risks include the stage-progression method's reliance on total-raised as a proxy and peer-median concentration in a small n=3 sample. The peer range itself ($3.1B–$10.3B) signals substantial heterogeneity within the same stage, underscoring that comparable multiples alone cannot resolve valuation with precision absent revenue disclosure or a detailed build-up.
